title: Reproducing Müller et al. 2023: wet oxidation of vertical Si and SiGe nanowires and nanosheets

sample.paper: “p-type silicon (Boron-doped at 1–2·10^19 cm−3)”; the Si wafer's orientation is not stated (Si(001) is stated only under the SiGe virtual substrates)
sample.ours: FAMILY: Si_Nanowire; ORIENTATION: Si100; DOPING: p_type_boron (recorded; no program reads it)
sample.note: Orientation (100) is ours; the appendix's bulk reference is labelled (100) in our transcription, not in the paper's text.

sample.paper: Vertical nanowires (round, star-shaped patterns) and nanosheets (2.1 µm long beams), “200 nm height”; as-etched diameters only on the x-axis of Figure 5
sample.ours: SHAPE: nanowire | nanosheet; DIAMETER_NM from Figure 5; HEIGHT_NM: 200 (recorded; no program reads it)
sample.note: The radial program treats a wire as an infinite cylinder: the top, the base and the 200 nm height do not enter. A nanosheet is stored with DIAMETER_NM and run as a cylinder.

sample.paper: “an enhanced oxide growth in the [110] and [−110] direction as compared to the [100] crystallographic direction, leading to a faceted appearance of large Si-NWs for an initial diameter of more than 60 nm”
sample.ours: not in our sample: one rate around the whole circumference
sample.note: Above 60 nm the paper's wires are faceted, not round; the oxide thickness is an average.

sample.paper: After the HF mask strip, a 20 W, 30 s oxygen plasma; the surface oxide at loading is not characterized. For the bulk references: “Samples were oxidized with an initial native oxide layer present, while any chemical oxide on Si samples was removed.”
sample.ours: the program starts the wire as bare silicon; it has no starting oxide
sample.note: Figure A1's bulk line extrapolates to about 9 nm at zero wet time, which the program's linear rate cannot have.

sample.paper: “non intentionally p-doped Si0.8Ge0.2 and Si0.5Ge0.5 virtual substrates”, graded at 10%/µm on Si(001), > 1 µm constant composition, “almost strain-free”
sample.ours: FAMILY: SiGe_oxide; COMPOSITION: Si0.80Ge0.20 | Si0.50Ge0.50; SUBSTRATE recorded
sample.note: No SiGe program reads strain, shape or size.

sample.paper: Blanket Si, Si0.8Ge0.2 and Si0.5Ge0.5 oxidized 2, 5 and 10 min in the same furnace; Si measured by ellipsometry, SiGe by cross-section SEM
sample.ours: the bulk slope is a parameter of the radial program (rate_planar); 19 nm bulk fixes the stored time
sample.note: The bulk samples are not samples in this study; they enter through the program's constants.

history.item: HSQ mask by e-beam lithography, then SF6/C4F8/O2 plasma etch, 200 nm tall
history.paper: “Samples are pre-cleaned with a 15 s oxygen plasma, directly followed by the main etching step using a gas mixture of SF6, C4F8 and O2 with constant pressure, power and overall flows.”
history.ours: SHAPE and DIAMETER_NM on the sample; the etch is not in our history

history.item: HSQ mask removed in diluted HF
history.paper: “Etched nanostructure samples are subsequently submerged in diluted hydrofluoric acid to remove the remaining HSQ mask”
history.note: HF concentration and time not stated.

history.paper: “followed by a low-power oxygen plasma cleaning (20 W for 30 s) to remove any carbon residues”
history.note: The vocabulary has no plasma clean. A 20 W oxygen plasma leaves a thin oxide on the sidewalls whose thickness the paper does not give; the radial program starts from bare silicon.

history.paper: “Nanostructures are characterized afterwards and also in between process steps by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) in a FEI Helios 600i.”
history.ours: DIAMETER_NM on the sample (the x-axis of Figure 5)

history.paper: “The 600 °C pre-heated oven is ramped up to 750 °C under nitrogen”
history.note: The gas and push rate at loading are not stated.

history.paper: “The 600 °C pre-heated oven is ramped up to 750 °C under nitrogen”
history.ours: RUN RampN2 DURATION 900 TEMP 600->750 AMBIENT inert_N2
history.note: Not in the stored recipe. 15 min (10 °C/min) is ours.

history.paper: “before the temperature is increased to the process temperature of 850 °C under a pure oxygen flow.”
history.ours: RUN RampO2 DURATION 600 TEMP 750->850 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: Not in the stored recipe. Dry oxide grows here before any steam. 10 min (10 °C/min) is ours.

history.paper: “After a thermalization period of 5 min, the oxygen flow is reduced and hydrogen injected”
history.ours: RUN Thermalize DURATION 300 TEMP 850->850 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: Not in the stored recipe. The gas during this hold is not restated; pure oxygen by context.

history.paper: “the oxygen flow is reduced and hydrogen injected, activating the oxidation process for the set time” (p. 3); “oxidation times were adjusted to grow 20 nm of oxide, e.g. 1.82 min for SiGe and 7.7 min for Si” (p. 12)
history.ours: RUN WetOxidation DURATION 462 TEMP 850->850 AMBIENT mix:H2O=0.95,O2=0.05
history.note: The stored recipe is one steam step of 779.5 s: the time the bulk slope of Figure A1 needs to reach 19 nm from zero. The paper's example is 7.7 min (462 s). The H2:O2 ratio is not stated; the steam fraction 0.95 is ours.

history.paper: “Then, the sample is cooled down under nitrogen.”
history.ours: RUN CoolN2 DURATION 1200 TEMP 850->600 AMBIENT inert_N2
history.note: Not in the stored recipe. Rate and unload temperature not stated; 20 min to 600 °C is ours.

history.paper: “The nanostructures have been observed by SEM and the increase of diameter/width for nanowires and nanosheets was measured as plotted in (a)”
history.ours: outer diameter = remaining core + 2 × oxide thickness

history.item: Oxide removed in buffered oxide etchant
history.paper: “The resulting oxide layer is afterwards removed by wet chemical etching in a buffered oxide etchant solution.”
history.note: Composition and time not stated; any silicon lost in the etch would count as consumed by oxidation.

history.paper: “samples are again observed by SEM with the shrunken nanostructure sizes plotted in (b).”
Si wires and Si sheets at one time; both SiGe compositions at another (“The choice of the same time for both SiGe substrates has been made for better comparison”)
history.ours: two furnace runs: each case names its run, and the alignment shares unknowns per run
history.note: That every Si structure was in one physical furnace load is our reading of “a set of test samples”.

history.paper: “Samples were fabricated using the same oxidation process as samples shown in figure 5 including the same nanostructures, only lacking large NW diameters.”
history.ours: the 55.6% germanium is compared on the largest SG20 sheet of Figure 5
history.note: The composition comes from a separate sample whose sheet width is not given.

steps.name: Etch
steps.label: HSQ mask by e-beam lithography, then SF6/C4F8/O2 plasma etch, 200 nm tall
steps.paper: “Samples are pre-cleaned with a 15 s oxygen plasma, directly followed by the main etching step using a gas mixture of SF6, C4F8 and O2 with constant pressure, power and overall flows.”
steps.timing: 15 s pre-clean stated; main etch time not stated

steps.name: Strip
steps.label: HSQ mask removed in diluted HF
steps.paper: “Etched nanostructure samples are subsequently submerged in diluted hydrofluoric acid to remove the remaining HSQ mask”

steps.name: Clean
steps.label: Oxygen plasma, 20 W, 30 s
steps.paper: “followed by a low-power oxygen plasma cleaning (20 W for 30 s) to remove any carbon residues”

steps.name: MeasureEtched
steps.label: As-etched diameter by SEM

steps.name: Load
steps.label: Into the furnace pre-heated to 600 °C
steps.paper: “The 600 °C pre-heated oven is ramped up to 750 °C under nitrogen”
steps.timing: Push rate and time at 600 °C before the ramp not stated

steps.name: RampN2
steps.label: Ramp 600 → 750 °C in nitrogen
steps.isl: RUN RampN2 DURATION 900 TEMP 600->750 AMBIENT inert_N2
steps.paper: “The 600 °C pre-heated oven is ramped up to 750 °C under nitrogen”
steps.timing: ramp rate not stated; 5 to 30 °C/min searched (5 to 30 min)

steps.name: RampO2
steps.label: Ramp 750 → 850 °C in pure oxygen
steps.isl: RUN RampO2 DURATION 600 TEMP 750->850 AMBIENT dry_O2
steps.paper: “before the temperature is increased to the process temperature of 850 °C under a pure oxygen flow.”
steps.timing: ramp rate not stated; 5 to 30 °C/min searched (200 to 1200 s)

steps.name: Thermalize
steps.label: Hold 5 min at 850 °C (oxygen)
steps.isl: RUN Thermalize DURATION 300 TEMP 850->850 AMBIENT dry_O2
steps.paper: “After a thermalization period of 5 min, the oxygen flow is reduced and hydrogen injected”
steps.timing: 5 min

steps.name: WetOxidation
steps.label: Steam at 850 °C, 7.7 min for Si
steps.isl: RUN WetOxidation DURATION 462 TEMP 850->850 AMBIENT mix:H2O=0.95,O2=0.05
steps.paper: “the oxygen flow is reduced and hydrogen injected, activating the oxidation process for the set time” (p. 3); “oxidation times were adjusted to grow 20 nm of oxide, e.g. 1.82 min for SiGe and 7.7 min for Si” (p. 12)
steps.timing: “e.g. 7.7 min for Si”, in the appendix only, as an example; counted from hydrogen injection

steps.name: CoolN2
steps.label: Cooled under nitrogen
steps.isl: RUN CoolN2 DURATION 1200 TEMP 850->600 AMBIENT inert_N2
steps.paper: “Then, the sample is cooled down under nitrogen.”
steps.timing: cool-down rate and unload temperature not stated
